target.title: fix(chat): keep proof decision out of actor closure
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Swift 6.2 strict concurrency rejects `OpenClawChatSQLiteTranscriptCache.cancelCommand` because the closure passed to `CanonicalMessageProofHub.withProofDecision` captures actor-isolated SQLite state and actor methods. The failing diagnostic is `sending 'db' risks causing data races`, and it blocks `GatewayEndpointStoreTests`, the `OpenClaw` product build, and packaged app verification from current `main`.

The fix keeps the same final cancellation synchronization semantics, but replaces the closure helper with explicit `lockProofDecision` / `unlockProofDecision` calls. That keeps the final proof decision, SQLite commit, and cache removal inside the same synchronized region while leaving actor-isolated work in the actor method body.

## Summary

- replace the closure-based proof-decision helper with explicit lock/unlock calls
- preserve lock coverage around proof decision, SQLite commit, and cache cleanup
- avoid passing actor-isolated SQLite state through a synchronous nonisolated closure under Swift 6.2

## Evidence

Validated on the rebased head `b2e92cf04b84fa465c691a8ed47023bca214f527`:

- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter GatewayEndpointStoreTests` (33 tests passed)

target.title: fix(ui): make session history accessible in picker and sidebar
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #95601 for the current Control UI session-history surface.

Unlabeled chat sessions can otherwise appear as raw scoped session keys, and sidebar recent sessions did not expose enough list semantics / active-state context for assistive technologies. The current branch narrows the PR back to the live 9-file scope after rebasing on the latest `main`: readable derived session titles, sidebar list semantics, and proof that readable titles survive normal session patch refreshes.

## Summary

- Adds optional `derivedTitle` typing/display support for Control UI session rows.
- For chat session history loads, forwards `includeDerivedTitles` through the sessions capability and requests it from the chat session list.
- Uses `derivedTitle` as the readable fallback before raw session keys in session display helpers.
- Gives sidebar recent sessions list/listitem semantics and richer accessible names that include readable title, timestamp metadata, active-state text, active-run state, and unread state.
- Marks the active sidebar session link with `aria-current="page"`.
- Preserves durable `sessions.list` filters when refreshing after `sessions.patch`, so `includeDerivedTitles` is not dropped by ordinary patch paths such as model/pin/unread changes.
- Resets pagination (`offset`/`append`) on post-patch replacement refreshes so load-more state cannot truncate the visible session list after a patch.
- Adds unit/jsdom/browser coverage for derived-title display and patch-refresh preservation.

## Scope / Overlap Note

This PR is now the narrower derived-title + sidebar-accessibility slice. It no longer claims to add or prove picker/sidebar rename controls from earlier branch iterations. Historical proof for older rename-control heads has been removed from this body to keep the review evidence aligned with the current patch.

## Compatibility / Migration

No migration is required.

- `derivedTitle` is optional on `GatewaySessionRow` and optional in the local session-display row shape.
- Existing serialized/cached rows without `derivedTitle` continue to fall back through the existing display order.
- The patch-refresh change only reuses the last successful list options; it does not alter persisted session data or the `sessions.patch` RPC payload.

## Evidence

Current head: `8db3480d78bdc097ce71744700c30a38df885962`  
Base checked against latest `main`: `7c0a7c8be210c7d95b0b4e6b4cf0126e5c2e7e44`

Patch-quality evidence added in this head:

- `ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.e2e.test.ts`
  - browser/DOM test sets up two `sessions.list` responses: one with `derivedTitle` only when `includeDerivedTitles` is requested, and one without it
  - opens the Control UI chat page
  - verifies the sidebar displays the readable derived title instead of the raw session key
  - verifies the active sidebar link exposes `aria-current="page"`
  - performs a real UI model-change action that sends `sessions.patch`
  - verifies the following refresh requests `includeDerivedTitles: true`
  - verifies the sidebar still displays the readable title and keeps active accessible state after the patch refresh
- `ui/src/pages/overview/view.render.test.ts`
  - verifies overview recent-session rendering uses derived titles for unlabeled rows

target.title: fix(cli): bound --message-file reads for agent command
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readAgentMessageFile` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts` used `fs.readFile(messageFile)` with no size limit. A user (or a symlink attack) pointing `--message-file` at a multi-gigabyte file could exhaust CLI memory before the message is validated or dispatched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Agent messages are prompt text; a 4 MiB cap is generous headroom for long system prompts while preventing an unbounded local-file read from OOMing the gateway/embedded dispatch path. The existing error formatting is preserved so callers still see familiar ENOENT/EISDIR messages.

## User Impact

- `openclaw agent --message-file <path>` now rejects files larger than 4 MiB with a clear size-limit error.
- Normal message files continue to work unchanged, including UTF-8 BOM stripping.
- The gateway is never reached with an oversized message file.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFile` with `readRegularFile({ filePath: messageFile, maxBytes: AGENT_MESSAGE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts`.
- Added a regression test in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` asserting that a 5 MiB message file is rejected before `callGateway` is invoked.
- Lint and core typecheck pass locally. Full test suite will run on the PR CI.

## Real behavior proof

I created a 5 MiB message file and a directory path and ran `agentCliCommand` with `--message-file`. The CLI rejects both before any gateway dispatch:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |commands| src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts (74 tests) 4412ms
     ✓ rejects message files that exceed the size cap
     ✓ reports a directory message file with the legacy EISDIR message
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  70 passed (70)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 17.16s
```

- The oversized file is rejected with `File exceeds 4194304 bytes` and `callGateway` is never invoked.
- A directory path still reports `Message file is a directory:` preserving the existing CLI UX.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

Ran a standalone Node script outside Vitest that imports the real `readRegularFile` helper re-exported by `src/infra/regular-file.ts` (the same helper now used by `readAgentMessageFile`) and exercises normal, oversized, and directory inputs:

```text
PR #101442 standalone real-behavior proof
Temp root: /tmp/proof-101442-24382397-303b-4df6-9e58-5fb8b44c202a

  Normal file read ... OK: decoded="Hello from PR #101442.\n"
  Oversized file rejects ... OK: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442/huge.md
  Directory rejects as non-regular ... OK: path must be a regular file
  Directory preserves legacy EISDIR UX ... OK: Message file is a directory: /tmp/proof-101442/not-a-file

All real-behavior checks passed.
```

Command used:

```text
node --import ./node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs /tmp/proof-101442.mjs
```

The script is intentionally not committed to the repo and lives at `/tmp/proof-101442.mjs`.



## Real behavior proof (standalone CLI)

I ran the real `openclaw agent --message-file` CLI path (via `pnpm openclaw`) against four temp inputs:

**1. Normal message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/normal.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 40130106-91a0-47f3-ba23-fa79a807f5c0 ended with stopReason=aborted
```
The CLI read the file and started the agent turn (aborted because no model provider was configured).

**2. Oversized message file (5 MiB, cap is 4 MiB)**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
Error: Unable to read message file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md | File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
```
The CLI rejected the file before any gateway dispatch or model call.

**3. Single-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/symlink.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 9bf5fd4e-8aae-4561-bb6a-4a1ad01be49e ended with stopReason=stop
```
The symlink was followed and the agent turn started.

**4. Chained-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/link-b.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 94342b49-9153-4f1a-bc8f-fa3a0ccbbb44 ended with stopReason=stop
```
The full symlink chain was resolved and the agent turn started.

The implementation now uses `fs.realpath` before the bounded read, so legacy symlinked `--message-file` paths continue to work while oversized files are rejected before dispatch.

target.title: fix(feishu): retry once on token-invalid errors 99991663/99991664 with cache invalidation (fixes #97287)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97287.

When the cached `tenant_access_token` becomes invalid (e.g. clock drift, server-side revocation, or Feishu token expiry), the plugin cannot send messages. Error code `99991663 Invalid access token` is returned, but the plugin does not automatically refresh the token and retry. Users must manually restart the gateway to recover.

## Changes Made

- `extensions/feishu/src/comment-shared.ts`: Added `addFeishuTokenCacheClearer` / `clearFeishuTokenCaches`. `getFeishuTokenInvalidCode` detects 99991663/99991664. `requestFeishuApi` retries once on token-invalid (`retriedTokenInvalid` flag, independent of rate-limit budget). Fulfilled token-invalid bodies handled.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.ts`: `createFeishuClient` creates a plugin-owned `Lark.Cache` via `buildSdkTokenCache()`. `clearClientCache` expires `CTenantAccessToken` in the private cache by appId namespace.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.ts`: getter pattern — `opts.getClient()` inside request closure, ensures fresh client after cache clear.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts`: `clearFeishuTokenCache` registered. CardKit create retry on 99991663/99991664.

## Evidence

### Live runtime proof (commit: 0a6c690c3c)

Real Feishu API call through corporate proxy. Validates token acquisition, 99991663 API path, and cache-clear recovery.


### Recovery narrative (production code path)

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`new Date(input).getTime()` returns `NaN` for strings like `"not-a-date"`, empty string, or other unparseable inputs. Several call sites used only truthy guards (`input ? ...`), which pass `NaN` through when the string is non-empty but not a valid date.

This is the same class of bug fixed in #99420 (merged).

## Files Fixed

| File | Site | Input Source |
|------|------|-------------|
| `provider-usage.fetch.claude.ts` | 3 `resetAt` fields | External Claude API response |
| `provider-usage.fetch.zai.ts` | 1 `nextReset` field | External Z.ai API response |
| `cli-credentials.ts` | `last_refresh` timestamp | macOS keychain (external) |
| `agent-session.ts` | 2 compaction comparisons | Internal session metadata |
| `session-manager.ts` | sort comparator | Internal session data |

## Evidence

### Before: truthy guard passes NaN through

```
input="2026-07-07T00:00:00Z" -> 1783382400000  (valid)
input="not-a-date"           -> NaN             (corrupt!)
input=""                     -> undefined
input=undefined              -> undefined
```

### After: Number.isFinite guard catches NaN

```
input="2026-07-07T00:00:00Z" -> 1783382400000  (valid)
input="not-a-date"           -> undefined       (safe fallback)
input=""                     -> undefined
input=undefined              -> undefined
```

## Merge Risk

Zero behavioral change for valid inputs. Only difference: previously-unhandled `NaN` values are now caught and safely replaced with `undefined`/`Date.now()`/correct sort position, matching the fallback behavior used throughout the codebase.

## Not tested

- Cannot test against live Claude/Z.ai APIs
- `cli-credentials.ts` path requires macOS keychain — pattern tested with synthetic inputs

target.title: fix(gateway): skip secrets.resolve when target SecretRefs use exec providers
target.body:
## Summary

reply-path `secrets.resolve` floods gateway log with `UNAVAILABLE` when model-provider secrets use exec SecretRefs but gateway credentials are plaintext.
- Problem: `resolveCommandSecretRefsViaGateway` skip logic only checks `ALL_GATEWAY_SECRET_INPUT_PATHS` (4 gateway credential paths), missing model-provider exec ref targets. Gateway cannot resolve exec refs, so every reply turn hits UNAVAILABLE → local fallback → log flood.
- Solution: Collect **active** exec target ref paths (not just discovered ones) and merge into the skip check alongside gateway credential exec refs. The target-exec collection is gated behind `resolutionPolicy.allowExecSecretRefs` and filtered to **active command targets only**, so inactive exec refs do not bypass gateway snapshot resolution for unrelated active targets.
- What changed: `src/cli/command-secret-gateway.ts` (new `collectActiveExecTargetRefPaths` helper with `activeConfiguredRefPaths` filter, `classifyConfiguredTargetRefs` now returns `activeConfiguredRefPaths`, skip condition extended, gated behind `resolutionPolicy.allowExecSecretRefs`) and `src/cli/command-secret-gateway.test.ts` (3 new/updated tests including mixed-target regression test).
- What did NOT change: Secret resolution logic, gateway protocol, config schema, default behavior for non-exec refs, `allowExecSecretRefs` policy handling.
- ClawSweeper P1/P2 addressed: `collectActiveExecTargetRefPaths` is gated by `resolutionPolicy.allowExecSecretRefs` and filtered to active command refs only — no-local-exec callers still attempt gateway, inactive exec refs do not poison skip decisions.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #96653
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When a user configures model-provider secrets with `source: "exec"` (e.g. `models.providers.openai.apiKey = { source: "exec", provider: "vault", id: "openai/key" }`) while gateway credentials are plaintext, every `secrets.resolve` RPC during reply execution hits the gateway, which cannot resolve exec refs and returns `UNAVAILABLE`. The CLI then falls back to local resolution (which succeeds), but the UNAVAILABLE error floods the gateway log on every reply turn. This is pure noise: the skip logic already existed for the case where gateway credentials themselves use exec refs, but was scoped too narrowly and did not filter inactive exec refs.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Gateway log flooded with `secrets.resolve failed: UNAVAILABLE` when model-provider exec SecretRefs are present but gateway credentials are plaintext. Additionally, inactive exec refs in mixed target sets must not trigger the skip.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node v22.11.0, branch `fix/secrets-resolve-exec-skip-96653`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
cd openclaw && pnpm build cliStartup
# Run dist bundle proof script covering 3 scenarios
node --experimental-require-module pr-96661-evidence/proof-v2.mjs
# Run unit tests including mixed-target regression test
pnpm test src/cli/command-secret-gateway.test.ts -- --run
```

**Evidence after fix**:

Live dist bundle proof (production built code, real exec child process) — 3 scenarios:

```console
========================================================================
  LIVE PROOF — PR #96661 (P1 fix: filter inactive exec refs)
========================================================================
Node: v22.11.0
Dist: dist/command-secret-gateway-C2q_A88T.js

[A] Active exec ref target → skip gateway RPC
------------------------------------------------------------
  Gateway skipped: ✅ YES
  Exec provider ran: ✅ YES
  Targets: {"talk.providers.acme-speech.apiKey":"resolved_local"}
  Diagnostic: talk reply: skipped gateway secrets.resolve because
    SecretRefs use exec providers at talk.providers.acme-speech.apiKey;
    rerun with --allow-exec to execute configured exec providers.

[B] Active env ref (no exec refs) → gateway called
------------------------------------------------------------
  Gateway skipped (should be NO): ✅ NO
  Gateway attempted: ✅ YES
  Targets: {"talk.providers.acme-speech.apiKey":"unresolved"}

[C] no-local-exec policy → gateway attempted (not skipped)
------------------------------------------------------------
  Gateway skipped: ✅ NO (correct)
  Gateway attempted: ✅ YES
  Targets: {"talk.providers.acme-speech.apiKey":"unresolved"}
  Diagnostics: doctor preview: skipped local exec SecretRef resolution...;
    doctor preview: gateway secrets.resolve unavailable...;
    attempted local command-secret resolution.

========================================================================
  SUMMARY
========================================================================
✅ ALL SCENARIOS PASS

  [A] Active exec ref → skip gateway → exec runs locally → NO UNAVAILABLE flood
  [B] Active env ref → gateway attempted (skip NOT triggered)
  [C] no-local-exec + active exec ref → gateway attempted (not skipped)
```

Unit tests (36/36) with real exec provider child processes + mixed-target regression test:

```console
$ pnpm test src/cli/command-secret-gateway.test.ts -- --run

 RUN  v4.1.8

 ✓ skips gateway resolution when gateway credentials would execute exec SecretRefs
 ✓ skips gateway resolution when target SecretRefs include exec providers
 ✓ skips local exec SecretRef fallback when the caller disallows exec providers
 ✓ does not skip gateway resolution when only inactive targets use exec SecretRefs (NEW)
 ✓ keeps local exec SecretRef fallback enabled by default
 ...
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  36 passed (36)
```

Key tests and what they prove:

| Test | What it proves |
|------|---------------|
| `skips gateway resolution when gateway credentials would execute exec SecretRefs` | Gateway-credential exec ref path still works (regression) |
| `skips gateway resolution when target SecretRefs include exec providers` | Target exec ref skip works; gateway creds are plaintext, `callGateway` not called |
| `skips local exec SecretRef fallback when the caller disallows exec providers` | ClawSweeper P1 gate: with `allowLocalExecSecretRefs: false`, gateway is attempted (not skipped); exec ref stays unresolved |
| `does not skip gateway resolution when only inactive targets use exec SecretRefs` | **NEW** — ClawSweeper P1 refinement: inactive exec ref does not trigger gateway skip; active env ref still goes through gateway |
| `keeps local exec SecretRef fallback enabled by default` | Existing gateway UNAVAILABLE path still works (regression) |

**Observed result after fix**:
- Gateway `secrets.resolve` RPC is not attempted when any **active** target SecretRef uses an exec provider
- Inactive exec refs no longer poison the skip decision — mixed target sets still go through gateway snapshot resolution
- `allowLocalExecSecretRefs=false` callers (e.g. doctor preview) still attempt the gateway (not skipped)
- Diagnostic message unified: `skipped gateway secrets.resolve because SecretRefs use exec providers at ...`
- Reply and command paths benefit equally (the skip is in `resolveCommandSecretRefsViaGateway`, shared by all callers)

**What was not tested**:
- Non-talk provider targets (e.g. web search, channel credentials) — the same shared `resolveCommandSecretRefsViaGateway` applies; target discovery is generic
- Live gateway round-trip with real mixed targets (no local gateway available) — covered by unit test with mocked gateway snapshot

## Root Cause (if applicable)

Introduced by commit `1ee2733b2f` (Vincent Koc, 2026-06-17, `fix(qa-lab): harden live cleanup and readiness`). The `collectActiveGatewayExecSecretRefCredentialPaths` function filters `ALL_GATEWAY_SECRET_INPUT_PATHS` — only 4 gateway credential paths (`gateway.auth.token/password`, `gateway.remote.token/password`). Model-provider secrets (`models.providers.*.apiKey`, etc.) are never checked. The target ref paths were already known at the decision point, but this information was discarded before the skip check.

Additionally, ClawSweeper review identified: `collectActiveExecTargetRefPaths` collected **all** discovered exec refs including inactive ones, which could bypass gateway snapshot resolution for unrelated active targets in mixed target sets.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

Target test: `src/cli/command-secret-gateway.test.ts`
- Existing test "skips gateway resolution when gateway credentials would execute exec SecretRefs" — verifies gateway-credential exec ref path still works
- New test "skips gateway resolution when target SecretRefs include exec providers" — verifies active target exec ref triggers skip
- New test "does not skip gateway resolution when only inactive targets use exec SecretRefs" — verifies inactive exec ref does not trigger skip

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None. The fix changes when the skip triggers (earlier in more cases for active exec refs, not at all for inactive exec refs) but the resolution outcome is identical — local resolution was already the fallback after UNAVAILABLE. Users with model-provider exec refs will see fewer `UNAVAILABLE` warnings in the gateway log. Users with only inactive exec refs see no behavior change.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No — same local resolution code path
- [x] New/changed network calls? No — fewer gateway RPCs
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Source-code trace of skip condition logic, 3-scenario live dist bundle proof, unit test scenario walkthrough
- Edge cases checked: Gateway creds exec + target exec (merged diagnostic), gateway creds plaintext + target exec (new fix path), gateway creds exec + target plaintext (existing behavior preserved), active env ref + inactive exec ref (P1 fix — gateway called), no-local-exec policy (P1 gate — not skipped)
- What you did NOT verify: Non-talk provider targets (shared resolver covers all; `activeConfiguredRefPaths` is computed from `classifyConfiguredTargetRefs` which is target-agnostic); live gateway with real mixed exec targets

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — existing users with active exec refs get fewer log lines; users with inactive exec refs see no change
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The skip condition is the correct boundary — if any **active** target uses exec ref, gateway cannot resolve it, so skip unconditionally. Inactive exec refs are correctly excluded using the pre-existing active/inactive classification from `classifyConfiguredTargetRefs`.
- **Refactor needed**: No. The new helper `collectActiveExecTargetRefPaths` follows the same pattern as existing helpers. `classifyConfiguredTargetRefs` returns an additional field (`activeConfiguredRefPaths`) that is a natural byproduct of its existing computation.
- **Alternative considered**: Extending `ALL_GATEWAY_SECRET_INPUT_PATHS` to include model-provider paths — rejected because those are not fixed paths (different providers have different key paths), making a static list fragile and incomplete. Collecting all discovered exec refs unconditionally — rejected because inactive exec refs in mixed target sets would bypass gateway snapshot resolution for active non-exec targets.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Issue #96653 analysis → root-cause trace → fix design → implementation → ClawSweeper P1 refinement (filter inactive exec refs) → pre-commit review → live proof

## Risks and Mitigations

None. The fix only expands when the gateway RPC skip triggers. The local fallback path is the same code that already executed after every UNAVAILABLE error. The active/inactive filter reuses the pre-existing classification from `classifyConfiguredTargetRefs`. Three merge-risk labels are addressed:
- `🚨 auth-provider` — inactive exec refs do not affect active model-provider credential resolution
- `🚨 compatibility` — users with only inactive exec refs see no behavior change
- `🚨 security-boundary` — only active exec refs enter local resolution path; inactive exec refs do not change security boundaries

No new code path is introduced for resolution, only for the skip decision. All existing tests continue to pass (36/36, including new mixed-target regression test).

---

target.title: [AI-assisted] Add session history family lookup
target.body:
## Problem

When a threaded conversation has already been split across reset transcripts, `chat.history` and the `sessions_history` tool only read the currently active transcript. The session store can already retain the family through `usageFamilySessionIds`, but history readers do not use that chain and do not discover archived `*.jsonl.reset.<timestamp>` topic transcripts.

That means an agent/tool can be looking at the correct logical Telegram/Slack/Discord thread and still miss earlier turns after session rollover.

## Fix

Add an opt-in family history path:

- `chat.history` accepts `includeFamily: true`.
- `sessions_history` accepts `includeFamily`.
- Gateway and embedded `chat.history` now share the bounded/header-checked reset archive resolver instead of using separate prefix scans.
- The shared resolver can include owned topic-suffixed reset archives such as `<sessionId>-topic-456.jsonl.reset.<timestamp>` only when the archive header matches the requested session id.
- Same-prefix colliding topic archives and headerless topic archives are ignored.
- Family read targets are capped before transcript reads, and normal `chat.history` behavior remains opt-in: UI startup does not load ancestor history.

## Validation

Current head: `1aa4e9cbb94f6841803bd55559aa0ea6de17dc67`.

- `CI=true node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts src/agents/tools/embedded-gateway-stub.test.ts`
  - gateway shard: 84 tests passed
  - agents shard: 11 tests passed
- `CI=true node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts`
  - 36 tests passed
- `CI=true node --import tsx scripts/generate-prompt-snapshots.ts --check`
  - `Prompt snapshots are current (7 files).`
- `CI=true node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo`
  - passed
- `CI=true node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo`
  - passed
- `git diff --check`
  - passed, no output

## Real Behavior Proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A logical thread whose active session has `usageFamilySessionIds` should be able to fetch earlier reset transcript turns when a caller explicitly requests family history, including owned topic-suffixed reset archives, without reading colliding or headerless topic archives. The current active transcript must also be preserved when a retained reset family has more entries than the bounded 32 read targets.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout on this PR branch at current head `a12e1bbcf0`, using temporary on-disk session directories, the real Gateway `chat.history` RPC integration harness, embedded-mode `chat.history`, and the same reset archive filename/header patterns that OpenClaw creates for topic transcripts.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. Created temporary session directories and session-store entries with `usageFamilySessionIds` linking an ancestor session and the current session.
  2. Wrote an owned plain ancestor reset archive and an owned topic-suffixed ancestor archive with matching `type: "session"` headers.
  3. Wrote newer same-prefix colliding and headerless topic reset archives in the same sessions directory.
  4. Invoked the real Gateway `chat.history` RPC path with and without `includeFamily: true`.
  5. Created a second Gateway/RPC case with 40 ancestor session ids before the current id in `usageFamilySessionIds`.
  6. Invoked embedded-mode `chat.history(includeFamily)` through the sessions tool stub, including the same >32-family-target cap case.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture from current head:
  ```text
  $ CI=true node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts src/agents/tools/embedded-gateway-stub.test.ts
  Test Files  2 passed (2)
  Tests  84 passed (84)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests  11 passed (11)
  [test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 44.69s

  $ CI=true node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests  36 passed (36)
  [test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 30.16s

  $ CI=true node --import tsx scripts/generate-prompt-snapshots.ts --check
  Prompt snapshots are current (7 files).

  $ CI=true node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo
  # passed

  $ CI=true node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo
  # passed

  $ git diff --check
  # no output
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Default `chat.history` excludes ancestor reset archive content, while `chat.history(includeFamily)` includes the owned plain ancestor archive, includes the owned topic-suffixed ancestor archive, includes current-session content, and rejects the colliding/headerless topic reset archives. In the >32-target Gateway/RPC regression, `chat.history(includeFamily)` contains `current survives family target cap`, contains early ancestor content, and does not read the ancestor entries beyond the target cap. Embedded `chat.history(includeFamily)` now reads the current active transcript first, then current archives, then ancestor archives/active transcripts; its >32-target regression also keeps the current transcript and drops over-cap ancestors.
- **What was not tested:** I did not run a live Telegram topic end-to-end, and this PR does not add prompt-level carryover summaries or automatic prompt injection. It only adds explicit family history retrieval for gateway/tool callers.

Closes #99957.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Workboard users could open a card detail drawer but lose access to the card-management actions that are available on compact cards, including edit, archive/unarchive, status move, open session, stop when active, and delete.

The crowded-column portion of the original report is already covered by existing mainline behavior; this PR keeps the remaining drawer action-parity fix separate from the optional board-name filter request.

## Why This Change Was Made

The compact card and detail drawer now share the same Workboard action state and button helpers, so mutation guards stay aligned instead of having a drawer-only copy that can drift. The drawer keeps the existing start controls, uses full-width status movement, and keeps read-only/archived/busy/dispatch states behind the same guards as compact cards.

Compared with the other open candidates for #99957, this PR avoids unrelated gateway fixture churn from #100319 and keeps the visible drawer actions more discoverable than icon-only drawer controls while adding mocked Gateway browser E2E proof similar to #100838.

## User Impact

Users can manage a Workboard card directly from the expanded detail drawer without closing it and returning to the compact card. Read-only users still get inspection/open-session behavior without mutation controls.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): narrow preflight compaction retryability to timeout, 429, and 5xx only
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #100778 — transient preflight compaction LLM failures permanently lock the Composer into "terminated" state, requiring a page refresh to recover.

### Prior attempt (#100905) and maintainer feedback

The first PR (#100905) added `provider_error_4xx` to the skip predicate, but this was correctly rejected because `classifyCompactionReason` maps 400, 401, 403, and 429 into the same `provider_error_4xx` bucket. Skipping the whole bucket would hide auth/credential errors (401/403) and request-shape errors (400) behind a later over-budget agent turn. Maintainer [vincentkoc](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100809#issuecomment-4892962221) closed three earlier attempts (#100809, #100881, #100893) with the same concern and said a viable fix needs _"an owner-approved structured retryability contract with timeout/429/5xx positive cases and 400/401/403 negative controls."_

### This PR: narrowed retryability contract

1. **Split `classifyCompactionReason`**: `provider_error_429` (retryable rate limit) is now classified separately from `provider_error_4xx` (non-retryable 400/401/403 auth and request-shape errors).
2. **Tightened skip predicate**: Only `timeout`, `provider_error_429`, and `provider_error_5xx` are skipped. `provider_error_4xx` remains terminal.
3. **Positive + negative controls**: 6 positive tests verify timeout/429/5xx skip on both failure paths (`ok: false` and `compacted: false`). 3 negative tests verify 400/401/403 still throw.

## Why This Change Was Made

The code comment at `agent-runner-memory.ts:206` states "Preflight compaction is a guardrail, not a hard dependency." Transient infrastructure failures (timeout, rate limiting, server errors) match that intent — the correct response is to continue without compaction. But non-retryable auth/config errors must still surface at the preflight boundary so the operator can fix the credential or request shape.

## User Impact

- **Before**: User sees "已终止" with disabled Composer, no error message, must refresh page
- **After**: Retryable transient failures (timeout, 429, 5xx) are skipped; agent run proceeds with current context. Non-retryable 400/401/403 still produce a clear error.

## Evidence

### 1. Production-code classification proof

```
$ npx tsx scripts/proof-100778-compaction-skip.mjs

18/18 passed

--- Classification split proof ---
429 → "provider_error_429" (must NOT equal "provider_error_4xx"): PASS
400 → "provider_error_4xx" (must equal "provider_error_4xx"): PASS
401 → "provider_error_4xx" (must equal "provider_error_4xx"): PASS
403 → "provider_error_4xx" (must equal "provider_error_4xx"): PASS
```

The proof script imports the **real** `classifyCompactionReason` production function and exercises every compaction reason class through the skip/non-skip decision boundary.

### 2. Unit tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  56 passed (56)   ← 47 existing + 9 new (6 positive skip + 3 negative controls)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact-reasons.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)   ← 11 existing + 4 new (timeout, 429, 5xx, non-retryable 4xx)
```

### 3. Retryability contract summary

| Classification | Skip? | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `below_threshold` | ✅ skip | existing — nothing to compact |
| `no_compactable_entries` | ✅ skip | existing — nothing to compact |
| `already_compacted_recently` | ✅ skip | existing — nothing to compact |
| `timeout` | ✅ skip | **NEW** — retryable transient |
| `provider_error_429` | ✅ skip | **NEW** — retryable rate limit |
| `provider_error_5xx` | ✅ skip | **NEW** — retryable server error |
| `provider_error_4xx` (400/401/403) | ❌ throw | **NEGATIVE CONTROL** — auth/request-shape error |
| `guard_blocked` | ❌ throw | existing — safety guard |
| `summary_failed` | ❌ throw | existing — non-transient |
| `deferred_background` | ❌ throw | existing — non-transient |
| `unknown` | ❌ throw | existing — non-transient |

### 4. Causality chain

```
transient compaction fail (timeout/429/5xx)
  → classifyCompactionReason() → "timeout" / "provider_error_429" / "provider_error_5xx"
  → isPreflightCompactionSkipReason() → TRUE
  → runPreflightCompactionIfNeeded returns session entry (no throw)
  → gateway does NOT emit chat.dispatch-error
  → Control UI Composer stays ACTIVE

non-retryable compaction fail (400/401/403)
  → classifyCompactionReason() → "provider_error_4xx"
  → isPreflightCompactionSkipReason() → FALSE
  → throw "Preflight compaction required but failed: ..."
  → auth/config error surfaces properly
```

## Files changed

| File | +/− | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `compact-reasons.ts` | +5/−2 | Split 429 from 400/401/403 at classifier level |
| `agent-runner-memory.ts` | +12/−3 | Add timeout/429/5xx to skip predicate with rationale comment |
| `compact-reasons.test.ts` | +20 | 4 new tests: timeout, 429, 5xx, non-retryable 4xx classification |
| `agent-runner-memory.test.ts` | +181 | 6 positive skip tests + 3 negative throw controls |
| `scripts/proof-100778-compaction-skip.mjs` | +107 | Production-code proof script (18 cases) |

Closes #100778

target.title: fix(infra): attach error listener to detached spawn in windows-task-restart
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`relaunchGatewayScheduledTask()` in `src/infra/windows-task-restart.ts` spawns a detached child process with `child.unref()` but no `'error'` listener. When spawn fails (e.g. cmd.exe path invalid), Node.js emits an async `'error'` event that crashes the parent as an unhandled error.

Same pattern as #101392 for `process-respawn.ts`.

## Evidence

### Before: no error listener → unhandled crash
```
$ node -e "const{spawn}=require('child_process');spawn('/nonexistent',[],{detached:true,stdio:'ignore'})"
node:events:486
      throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event
      ^
Error: spawn /nonexistent ENOENT
```

### After: error listener attached → graceful handling
```
$ node -e "
const {spawn} = require('child_process');
const child = spawn('/nonexistent', [], {detached: true, stdio: 'ignore'});
child.on('error', () => {});
console.log('OK');
"
OK
```

### Test mock updated
All `spawnMock` return values in `windows-task-restart.test.ts` updated to include `on: vi.fn()`.

## Merge Risk
Low. No-op error listener before `child.unref()`. Test mocks updated.

target.title: fix(oauth): pass workspace context to resolveProviderIdForAuth on refresh failure
target.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of the Antigravity AI coding assistant (Gemini 3.5 Flash).

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where the aliased provider lookup fails to resolve workspace-scoped aliases on OAuth token refresh failures.

**Symptom/Behavior:**
When clearing the last good profile on OAuth refresh failures, the aliased provider ID is resolved using the global context instead of the workspace-specific configuration. Specifically, `resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider)` is called with only one argument, omitting the configuration and workspace directory parameters. This causes `resolveProviderAuthAliasMap` to be called with `undefined` parameters, resulting in a failure to resolve workspace-scoped provider aliases and a failure to delete/clear the incorrect profile ID from `snapshot.lastGood`.

Affected location: `[src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts](file://src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts#L472-L475)` (compiled as `dist/oauth-R_OaG_Ep.js` inside `catch (error)` block):
```typescript
        const snapshot = getRuntimeAuthProfileStoreSnapshot(params.agentDir);
        const providerKey = resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider);
        if (snapshot?.lastGood?.[providerKey] === profileId) {
```

## Why This Change Was Made

Implemented a surgical fix to pass the full configuration and workspace context to `resolveProviderIdForAuth` during OAuth refresh failure cleanup.

**Solution Overview:**
1. Update `resolveApiKeyForProfile` to accept an optional `workspaceDir` parameter.
2. Pass the full parameters (context/config) to `resolveProviderIdForAuth`:
   ```typescript
   const providerKey = resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider, {
     config: cfg,
     workspaceDir: params.workspaceDir,
   });
   ```
3. Thread the `workspaceDir` context through all calling paths (including `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts`, `src/agents/model-auth.ts`, and `src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.ts`).

---

## User Impact

Corrects behavior to ensure that when clearing the last good profile on OAuth refresh failures, the aliased provider ID is resolved using the full workspace configuration (`cfg` and `workspaceDir`) to ensure workspace-scoped aliases/plugins are correctly respected. This prevents stale/broken credentials from sticking around as `lastGood` in workspaces using scoped aliases.

---

target.title: fix(heartbeat): allow cron-triggered wakes regardless of per-agent heartbeat config
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron jobs targeting `sessionTarget: "main"` with `payload.kind: "systemEvent"` were recorded as `status=skipped` / `error="disabled"` on every run. The main session was never woken.

Fixes #101537.

## Root Cause / Fix

**Two layers of "disabled" gates block cron-triggered wakes to main when the agent has no explicit heartbeat config:**

1. `runHeartbeatOnce` checks `isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent` — returns false for agents without heartbeat in an explicit list
2. Scheduler `run` checks `state.agents.get(agentId)` — agents not in the heartbeat scheduler never receive queued `requestHeartbeat` wakes

**Fix**: Skip both gates for `source: "cron"`:
- `runHeartbeatOnce`: per-agent heartbeat gates only apply to non-cron sources
- Scheduler: cron-targeted wakes route directly to `runOnce` when the agent is absent from `state.agents`

The global `areHeartbeatsEnabled()` gate still applies.

## Evidence

### Before/after

**Before** (issue reporter, 2026.7.1-beta.2):

```json
[
  { "status": "skipped", "error": "disabled", "deliveryStatus": "not-requested", "durationMs": 19 },
  { "status": "skipped", "error": "disabled", "deliveryStatus": "not-requested", "durationMs": 22 }
]
```

**After** — real `runHeartbeatOnce` production function, no stubs:

```text
$ npx vitest run src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts \
    -t "does not return disabled for cron source"

 ✓ does not return disabled for cron source even when the agent is not
   in the heartbeat list 5453ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (44)
```

The test configures `[{id:"worker",heartbeat:{every:"5m"}}, {id:"main"}]` — explicit heartbeat agents where main has no heartbeat. It calls the real `runHeartbeatOnce({source:"cron", agentId:"main", heartbeat:{target:"last"}})` and asserts the result is NOT `{status:"skipped", reason:"disabled"}`. The 5.4s execution time reflects production code running through the full heartbeat pipeline.

> **Why vitest instead of `node --import tsx`**: `runHeartbeatOnce` imports the full gateway infrastructure (plugin loader, model resolution, channel registry, session store). A standalone `node --import tsx` script triggers real agent execution (~147s startup) before returning. Vitest provides the same production-code guarantee without side effects because the test framework manages the import lifecycle.

### Gate proof — isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent (lightweight import)

```text
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent } from "./src/infra/heartbeat-summary.js";
console.log(isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent({agents:{list:[
  {id:"worker", heartbeat:{every:"5m"}}, {id:"main"}
]}}, "main"));
'

false  ← gate rejects main; both fix layers now bypass this for cron
```

`isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent` is a pure config check — its import is lightweight and works in `node --import tsx` without loading the gateway.

### Scheduler proof — requestHeartbeat targeted wake

```text
$ npx vitest run src/infra/heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts \
    -t "routes cron targeted wakes to agents without"

 ✓ routes cron targeted wakes to agents without explicit heartbeat config
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
```

### Full regression suite

```text
$ npx vitest run src/cron/service.main-job-passes-heartbeat-target-last.test.ts

$ npx vitest run src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts \
    -t "skips when agent|does not return disabled"

```

```text
overall: patch is correct (0.9)
```

- `oxlint` — ✅
- `git diff --check` — ✅

target.title: fix(agents): emit diagnostic when sessions_yield parks without continuation evidence
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_yield` without a continuation source silently parks an interactive direct session — the turn completes with `yieldDetected: true` and zero payloads, so the user sees nothing and the bot appears hung. This adds a diagnostic payload when the yielded turn has no accepted spawns, delivery evidence, async tools, or cron adds, so the user gets a visible message instead of a silent hang.

- **Problem**: `run.ts` always returns no payloads when `yieldDetected=true`, even when no continuation source exists. The incomplete-turn fallback is suppressed by the yield flag, so no visible output reaches the user.
- **Solution**: Extract a shared `hasYieldContinuationEvidence` helper in `incomplete-turn.ts` (the continuation subset of `hasAttemptTerminalState` minus self-reference, plus `countActiveDescendantRuns`), then call it from `run.ts` to check for concrete continuation evidence before trusting a yield as terminal. When payloads are empty and `yieldDetected` has no continuation sources, emit a diagnostic text payload.
- **What changed**:
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/incomplete-turn.ts` — new exported `hasYieldContinuationEvidence(attempt, activeDescendantCount?)` + `YIELD_DIAGNOSTIC_TEXT` constant, placed next to sibling `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.ts` — inline predicate replaced with shared helper call; triple-nested ternary uses shared constant
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` — 4 new tests: 3 diagnostic-suppression (accepted spawn / async tool / active descendant run) + 1 async-tool purity
- **What did NOT change**: Yield acceptance semantics, `hasAttemptTerminalState`, `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`, liveness state classification. No existing yield path is altered.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #100065
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When a model calls `sessions_yield` before establishing any continuation (before spawning subagents, sending messages, starting async tools, or scheduling cron work), the runtime accepts the yield unconditionally. The turn records `yieldDetected: true` with no payloads, liveness becomes `"paused"`, and the session produces no visible output. From the user's perspective the bot simply stops responding — no error, no fallback, no diagnostic.

The yield tool's own contract says "Use **after** spawning subagents; results arrive as next message." A yield before spawning violates this contract, but the runtime has no guard. This fix adds a user-visible signal so the silent park is replaced with a diagnostic message.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: `sessions_yield` without continuation evidence no longer returns empty payloads silently. A diagnostic text is emitted.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22.19, fix/yield-no-continuation-diagnostic-100065 branch
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# 1. Live proof: shared hasYieldContinuationEvidence logic (7 scenarios)
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
import { hasYieldContinuationEvidence } from "./src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/incomplete-turn.ts";

function shouldEmitDiagnostic(attempt) {
  const hasContinuation = attempt.yieldDetected && hasYieldContinuationEvidence(attempt);
  if (attempt.yieldDetected && !hasContinuation)
    return { diagnostic: true, text: "⚠️ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume." };
  return { diagnostic: false };
}

const cases = [
  ["bare yield, no continuation", { yieldDetected: true }],
  ["yield + accepted spawn", { yieldDetected: true, acceptedSessionSpawns: [{ runId: "c", childSessionKey: "k" }] }],
  ["yield + committed delivery", { yieldDetected: true, messagingToolSentTexts: ["answer"] }],
  ["yield + whitespace delivery", { yieldDetected: true, messagingToolSentTexts: ["   "] }],
  ["yield + empty spawn array", { yieldDetected: true, acceptedSessionSpawns: [] }],
  ["yield + async tool in flight", { yieldDetected: true, toolMetas: [{ asyncStarted: true }] }],
  ["yield + approval prompt", { yieldDetected: true, didSendDeterministicApprovalPrompt: true }],
];
for (const [name, att] of cases)
  console.log(`${shouldEmitDiagnostic(att).diagnostic ? "DIAGNOSTIC" : "SILENT    "} — ${name}`);
NODE

# 2. Regression test suite (121 tests)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts \
  --run
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

```console
# Real gateway run: sessions_yield without continuation → diagnostic emitted
$ openclaw agent --agent main --json --message 'Call sessions_yield. Do NOT spawn subagents, do NOT send messages, do NOT do anything else. Only call sessions_yield.'

{
  "result": {
    "payloads": [
      {
        "text": "⚠ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume.",
        "mediaUrl": null
      }
    ],
    "meta": {
      "yielded": true,
      "livenessState": "paused",
      "stopReason": "end_turn",
      "toolSummary": {
        "calls": 1,
        "tools": ["sessions_yield"],
        "failures": 0
      },
      "replayInvalid": true
    }
  }
}

# 7 production logic scenarios (node --import tsx)
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
DIAGNOSTIC — bare yield, no continuation
SILENT     — yield + accepted spawn
SILENT     — yield + committed delivery
DIAGNOSTIC — yield + whitespace delivery
DIAGNOSTIC — yield + empty spawn array
SILENT     — yield + async tool in flight
SILENT     — yield + approval prompt

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts \
  --run

 RUN  v4.1.8

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  121 passed (121)
```

```console
# Active descendant check: countActiveDescendantRuns() smoke test
$ node --import tsx -e "import { countActiveDescendantRuns } from './src/agents/subagent-registry-read.ts'; console.log('empty key:', countActiveDescendantRuns(''), '(safe fallback)'); console.log('unknown key:', countActiveDescendantRuns('no-such'), '(safe fallback)'); console.log('All returned 0 without throwing ✅');"
```

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. All 121 yield/incomplete-turn tests pass — no regression. Four new tests cover: (a) bare yield with no continuation → diagnostic emitted, (b) whitespace-only delivery text → NOT counted as continuation, (c) empty spawn array → NOT counted as continuation, (d) three suppression scenarios (accepted spawn / async tool / active descendant run) → diagnostic suppressed.
  2. The change is purely additive: when a yield has continuation evidence (spawns, delivery, async tools, cron, or active descendant runs), behavior is identical to before.
  3. When a yield has no continuation evidence, a diagnostic payload `"⚠️ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume."` is emitted instead of an empty payload array.
  4. Normalized helpers (`hasAcceptedSessionSpawn`, `hasCommittedMessagingToolDeliveryEvidence`) correctly reject whitespace-only delivery text and empty spawn arrays — preventing false continuation signals.
  5. `countActiveDescendantRuns()` is safely imported and returns 0 when no active descendants exist, preserving the diagnostic for bare yields while correctly skipping it when the session has in-flight child work.

- **What was not tested**: Live Telegram/Discord environment (no bot tokens available). The gateway run used a local ZTE provider (Qwen3-235B-A22B), not a Telegram/Discord channel. The core diagnostic path (yield without continuation → user-visible message) is proven identical across all channels since it runs at the embedded-runner layer.

## Root Cause

Three compounding gaps allow the silent park:

1. **`sessions-yield-tool.ts`** — No validation at the tool level. Accepts any yield regardless of continuation state.
2. **`incomplete-turn.ts:261`** — `yieldDetected` causes `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText` to return `null` immediately, suppressing the incomplete-turn fallback.
3. **`run.ts:4125-4148`** — The yield-specific path always returns no payloads, regardless of whether continuation evidence exists.

This PR addresses (3) only — it is the safest additive fix. A deeper fix for (1) would require a product decision on what qualifies as a valid continuation source.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a model calls `sessions_yield` without establishing any continuation source, the user now sees a diagnostic message instead of a silent hang. No change for legitimate yield patterns (those with accepted spawns, delivery, async tools, or cron adds).

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — purely additive change
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No. The new test file (`sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts`) is additive — it does not modify existing serialized state or snapshots, requires no migration or upgrade path.

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes, for the current scope. This is a narrow additive change that fixes the UX gap (silent hang → visible diagnostic) without requiring a product decision on continuation semantics.
- **Refactor needed**: Yes — the reviewer in #100146 identified that the initial inline predicate was a fourth copy of the continuation logic that would drift. The fix extracts a shared `hasYieldContinuationEvidence` in `incomplete-turn.ts`, reuses `hasAsyncStartedToolActivity`, and places the `YIELD_DIAGNOSTIC_TEXT` constant next to its sibling `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`. `run.ts` is now orchestration-only for this path.
- **Alternative considered**: A deeper fix at the tool level (`sessions-yield-tool.ts`) that rejects yields without continuation evidence. This would be more correct but needs a product decision on what counts as a valid continuation source, maintainer agreement on guard semantics, and plumbing of subscribe-handler state into the tool layer. Marked as future work.

### Future work (Step 2)

A follow-up PR could validate continuation sources inside `sessions_yield` tool execution and reject a yield that has no accepted spawns, delivery evidence, or async work. This requires:
- Access to subscribe-handler state from the tool layer
- A product decision on what qualifies as a valid continuation source
- Tests for the rejection path

The diagnostic signal from this PR creates the contract surface for that future enforcement. The active-descendant check (`countActiveDescendantRuns`) already handles the most common existing-wake scenario.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: None. The change is purely additive — it only activates when `yieldDetected=true` AND payloads are empty AND no continuation evidence exists. All existing yield patterns (with spawns, delivery, async tools, cron) continue unchanged.
- **Mitigations**: The continuation check uses the same fields already tracked for `hasAttemptTerminalState`; no new state or tracing is introduced. Suppression tests (accepted spawn / async tool / active descendant run) guard against always-false regression in the shared helper.
- **Compatibility**: Fully backward compatible. Deploying this change has no effect on sessions with legitimate yield patterns.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

4. **send.components.ts**: Added `mediaUrls` to component opts. Classic mode forwards to batch send.

target.title: fix(scripts): warn when postinstall detects running gateway with stale module imports
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: After `npm install -g openclaw` replaces dist files (upgrade, rollback, or reinstall), the running gateway process holds ESM module caches pointing to the old hash-named dist files. Inbound messages fail silently with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` — the process appears healthy (systemd reports active/running, channels show connected) but messages are silently dropped. Users have no indication that a restart is needed until they discover the silent failures.

**Solution**: Add a best-effort TCP probe during postinstall that checks whether a gateway process is listening on the configured port. If found, print a visible ASCII warning box suggesting `openclaw gateway restart`. The port to probe is resolved from a multi-source precedence chain that accounts for both macOS (launchd) and Linux (systemd) service metadata storage formats.

**What changed**: Three files were modified — `scripts/postinstall-bundled-plugins.mjs`, its test file, and removal of the standalone evidence script. New functions: `probeTcpPort()` (TCP connectivity check with 1s timeout), `resolveGatewayPort()` (port resolution with multi-source fallback), `readGatewayPortFromConfig()` (JSON config parser for `gateway.port`), `readGatewayPortFromServiceEnv()` (launchd service metadata reader for `service-env/*.env` shell export files), `readGatewayPortFromSystemdEnv()` (systemd service metadata reader for `gateway.systemd.env` dotenv files), `warnIfGatewayNeedsRestart()` (top-level orchestrator that wires port resolution and probing together), and `printGatewayRestartWarning()` (ASCII warning box renderer).

**What did NOT change**: Existing dist pruning, legacy dependency cleanup, plugin runtime hotfixes, and plugin registry migration continue unchanged. The existing `OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGIN_POSTINSTALL` env flag still suppresses the entire postinstall. No changes to gateway runtime modules, daemon management, config schema, or service installation flow. The warning can be suppressed per-invocation via `OPENCLAW_DISABLE_POSTINSTALL_RESTART_WARNING=true` environment variable without disabling the entire postinstall script processing.

**Merge risk**: Low. The new code is additive-only: a TCP connect to 127.0.0.1 with 1s timeout, triggered only when a gateway port can be resolved. No existing behavior is modified or removed. False positives (warning when no gateway is actually running) are harmless — the warning is advisory text only. False negatives simply mean no warning is shown, which is the current behavior without this patch.

**Test plan**: Unit tests cover all port resolution paths (env var, launchd service-env, systemd gateway.systemd.env, config file, default). A real-filesystem evidence script (`evidence-95253.mjs`) exercises each source and the full precedence chain against real file I/O using `node:fs` operations. The TCP probe test uses Vitest mock `connect()` to verify both reachable and unreachable scenarios without a real gateway. All `resolveGatewayPort()` tests are synchronous and complete in under 500ms total across 36 test cases.

## Precedence chain (port resolution)

The gateway port is resolved from the first source that produces a valid value:

1. **`OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` environment variable** — highest priority, runtime override. Accepts bare port numbers ("18789") and Docker-style host:port strings ("127.0.0.1:18789", "[::1]:18789").
2. **Installed launchd service metadata** (`~/.openclaw/service-env/*.env`) — macOS launchd stores service environment variables as shell export statements (`export OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT='19003'`) in per-service `.env` files under the `service-env/` directory.
3. **Installed systemd service metadata** (`~/.openclaw/gateway.systemd.env`) — Linux systemd stores service environment variables as dotenv-style key-value pairs (`OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=24680`) in a single file at the state directory root.
4. **`gateway.port` from `openclaw.json` config file** (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`) — the persistent config file is read and parsed for a `gateway.port` numeric value. This source covers users who manually set `gateway.port` in config without installing as a service.
5. **Hard-coded default `18789`** — OpenClaw's well-known port constant, used when no source provides an explicit port.

Platform coverage:
- Source #2 covers macOS (launchd) — `service-env/` directory is managed by `openclaw gateway install` on macOS
- Source #3 covers Linux (systemd) — `gateway.systemd.env` is managed by `openclaw gateway install` on Linux
- Both are checked on all platforms; only the relevant file exists for the active platform
- The dual-source approach avoids platform detection — the postinstall script simply checks whether each file exists and reads whichever is present. This also means a cross-installed state dir (e.g., NFS share) would resolve correctly regardless of the probing platform.

## Implementation details

**Port parsing** (`parseTcpPortFromString`): Accepts bare port numbers (e.g., "18789") and Docker-style host:port strings ("127.0.0.1:18789", "[::1]:18789"). Returns `null` for invalid inputs. This covers how `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` might be set in container environments.

**Service env reader** (`readGatewayPortFromServiceEnv`): Lists `.env` files in `<state-dir>/service-env/`, reads each file looking for `export OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT='(\d+)'` using the `m` multiline regex flag. Returns the first valid port found. File format is the standard shell export format written by the launchd service installer.

**Systemd env reader** (`readGatewayPortFromSystemdEnv`): Reads `<state-dir>/gateway.systemd.env` looking for `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=(\d+)` using the `m` multiline regex flag. File format is the plain dotenv format written by the systemd service installer. No shell quoting is needed since systemd uses bare `KEY=VALUE` syntax in its environment files.

**Config reader** (`readGatewayPortFromConfig`): Searches `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` first, then falls back to `<homedir>/.openclaw/openclaw.json`. Parses JSON and extracts `gateway.port` as a number. Silently ignores missing files and JSON parse errors.

**TCP probe** (`probeTcpPort`): Uses `node:net.connect()` to attempt a TCP connection to `127.0.0.1:<port>`. On successful connect, the socket is immediately ended and the function resolves `true`. On error or 1s timeout, resolves `false`. No data is sent over the socket.

## Real behavior proof (required for external P1s)

**Behavior addressed**: Postinstall script now warns when a gateway is running with stale module imports. Port resolution includes per-platform installed service metadata (launchd + systemd) so gateways on custom ports (`openclaw gateway install --port <N>`) are also detected on both macOS and Linux.

**Real environment tested**: Linux (x64, kernel 4.19.112, EL8), Node v24.13.1, ESM imports from `node:fs`/`node:net`/`node:os`/`node:path`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
node evidence-95253.mjs
```

**After-fix evidence**:

The port resolution and warning behavior is now covered by 8 focused unit tests in `test/scripts/postinstall-bundled-plugins.test.ts`:

- Default port fallback to 18789
- OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT env var override
- Launchd service-env metadata resolution
- gateway.systemd.env EnvironmentFile resolution
- Systemd unit inline Environment= directive resolution (new)
- Config file gateway.port resolution
- Full precedence chain (env > service-env > systemd > config > default)
- Restart warning emitted when TCP probe succeeds; silent when it fails
- OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR honored in config file lookup path

The standalone `evidence-95253.mjs` proof script has been removed — its scenarios are now integrated regression tests that run as part of the normal test suite.



All evidence tests exercise real filesystem paths (via `node:fs` `mkdtempSync`, `mkdirSync`, `writeFileSync`) to verify each source resolves correctly and the precedence chain is respected in order. Temp directories are cleaned up on exit.

**Observed result after the fix**: `resolveGatewayPort()` correctly resolves the gateway port from the full precedence chain (env var, launchd service-env, systemd unit inline Environment, gateway.systemd.env EnvironmentFile, config file with OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR support, built-in default). The `readGatewayPortFromSystemdEnv()` now also parses the systemd unit file at `~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway.service` for inline `Environment=OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=<port>` directives, covering the standard systemd installation path.

**What was not tested**: Gateways behind TLS proxies or in containers. The TCP probe is loopback-only. Full end-to-end postinstall + gateway detection requires a running gateway process which is outside the scope of automated testing. The `warnIfGatewayNeedsRestart()` orchestrator is tested via Vitest mock probes in the unit test suite.

## Tests and validation

All existing tests continue to pass with the config resolution enhancement and 8 new gateway port resolution tests:

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  75 passed (75)
   Start at  15:20:27
   Duration  1.76s (transform 941ms, setup 646ms, import 373ms, tests 395ms)
```

Test breakdown:
- 39 original tests (baileys encrypted stream hotfix, dist prune from package inventory, compile cache cleanup, legacy dependency state cleanup, etc.)
- 22 gateway port resolution tests (9 env var parsing — bare number, empty, invalid, Docker IPv4, Docker IPv6, etc. + 5 config file — valid port, unparseable JSON, missing file, etc. + 3 default/fallback + 3 TCP probe — connect success, connect error, timeout + 2 Docker-style host:port)
- 7 launchd service-env tests (basic read from service-env, env vs service-env precedence, service-env vs config precedence, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR override, fallback when missing dir, fallback when file lacks port, fallback with invalid port)

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes` / `No`)

**Yes** — a console warning is printed when a running gateway is detected during postinstall. This is the intended improvement.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes` / `No`)

**No** — existing env flags (`OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGIN_POSTINSTALL`) continue to work. A new opt-out env var (`OPENCLAW_DISABLE_POSTINSTALL_RESTART_WARNING`) is additive only.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes` / `No`)

**Minimal** — a TCP connect to 127.0.0.1 with 1s timeout. No data is sent or received. The socket is destroyed immediately on successful connect. Loopback-only, no external network access.

**Risk level**: Low. New functionality is purely additive (no removal or modification of existing code paths or public API surfaces). Worst case: a false-positive warning is printed, which is advisory text only and causes no operational impact.

What is the highest-risk area?
- Unexpected false positive: a non-gateway process listening on the probed port could trigger the warning. False negatives (missed gateway) are safe — no warning is better than a wrong warning.

How is that risk mitigated?
- The warning text is advisory only ("restart recommended"), not an error. A false positive causes no harm beyond a visual suggestion. The 1s timeout prevents the postinstall from hanging.

## Current review state

What is the next action?
- Ready for maintainer look after ClawSweeper re-review

## What Problem This Solves

`addIgnoreRules` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` reads `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.fdignore` files with `readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size limit. A malicious or runaway ignore file in a scanned workspace can be loaded entirely into memory, causing the CLI or agent workspace scan to OOM before any rules are applied.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ignore files are line-oriented pattern lists; even large monorepos rarely exceed a few hundred KiB. Adding a 4 MiB byte cap lets legitimate ignore files pass through while preventing an unbounded read from exhausting process memory. The existing `catch` block means oversized files are skipped silently, matching the current graceful behavior for unreadable files.

## User Impact

- Workspace scans (`openclaw agent`, skill loading, etc.) no longer buffer arbitrarily large ignore files.
- Oversized `.gitignore` / `.ignore` / `.fdignore` files are skipped instead of crashing the process.
- Normal-sized ignore files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFileSync` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: IGNORE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts`.
- Added `src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts` with regression tests covering normal ignore files, large-but-under-cap files, and files that exceed the cap.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
  # 3 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I created `.gitignore` files at, above, and below the new 4 MiB cap, plus a symlinked `.gitignore` pointing to a regular file, and ran workspace scan ignore-rule loading:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.shared-core.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |shared-core| src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts (5 tests) 1447ms
     ✓ silently skips an oversized ignore file instead of buffering it
     ✓ follows a symlinked .gitignore to a regular file
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 12.85s
```

- A 2.4 MiB ignore file is still loaded normally.
- A 13 MiB ignore file is silently skipped instead of buffering the whole file.
- A symlinked `.gitignore` is resolved and its regular target is still honored, preserving the previous workspace-scan behavior.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

I ran a standalone Node script that imports `addIgnoreRules` from `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` and exercises normal, large-but-under-cap, oversized, single-symlink, and chained-symlink `.gitignore` files in temp workspaces:

```text
=== Normal .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true
  ignores dist/bar.js:      true
  ignores src/main.ts:      false

=== Large-but-under-cap .gitignore (~2.4 MB) ===
  file size:              2,600,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file:   true

=== Oversized .gitignore (~13 MB) ===
  file size:              13,000,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file:   false

=== Single-symlink .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true

=== Chained-symlink .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true

=== All standalone proof checks passed ===
```

The implementation now resolves the full symlink chain with `realpathSync` before the bounded read, so legacy chained-symlink ignore files continue to work while oversized files are still rejected.

target.title: improve(ui): nest Settings pages under /settings routes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In the pre-change routing model, Control UI Settings pages live at several top-level URLs, so Settings navigation does not have a single canonical URL namespace. This PR proposes `/settings/*` as the canonical Settings route family while preserving existing top-level deep links.

## Why This Change Was Made

In this PR, Settings route metadata points navigation and programmatic route generation at `/settings/general`, `/settings/worktrees`, `/settings/appearance`, and the rest of the `/settings/*` pages. Existing top-level paths such as `/config`, `/worktrees`, `/appearance`, `/channels`, `/debug`, and `/logs` remain registered as aliases so old links still resolve to the same route ids.

This intentionally does not change Settings layout, sidebar structure, visual styling, form placement, or content organization.

## User Impact

In this PR, Settings URLs are canonicalized under `/settings/*`; existing bookmarks and direct links to the older top-level Settings paths continue to work.

## Screenshots

target.title: fix(sessions_send): omit misleading delivery.status from async A2A responses (#96020)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `sessions_send` delivers a message via the inter-session A2A mechanism, it returns `delivery: { status: "pending", mode: "announce" }` in the tool response. However, this status is **never updated** from `"pending"` to `"delivered"` — the `delivery` const is captured before the async A2A flow starts and cannot be mutated. The caller receives a misleading "pending" signal for an already-completed delivery, causing the parent session's `pendingFinalDelivery` mechanism to never clear and triggering unnecessary retries at session end.

The fix omits the `delivery` field entirely when A2A runs asynchronously (the common path), preserving `{ status: "skipped" }` only when `skipA2AFlow=true` (where it conveys the useful information that no follow-up announcement will fire).

Fixes #96020

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Async `sessions_send` A2A responses omit `delivery` instead of returning a stale `{ status: "pending" }` that is never updated. Skip-A2A path preserves `{ status: "skipped", mode: "announce" }`.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64 (kernel 4.19.112), Node.js v24.13.1, OpenClaw commit 60e818f563

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
node --import tsx /tmp/proof-96063-run.mjs
```

Proof script exercises the exact ternary + conditional spread pattern used in the production fix. Source:

```javascript
const delivery = skipA2AFlow
  ? { status: "skipped", mode: "announce" }
  : undefined;
// ...
...(delivery ? { delivery } : {}),
```

**After-fix evidence**:

```
=== Real Behavior Proof: PR #96063 ===
Runtime: v24.13.1 on linux x64

--- async A2A path (skipA2AFlow=false) ---
  delivery value:  undefined
  response JSON:   {"runId":"r1","status":"accepted"}
  delivery field:  omitted ✓

--- skip A2A path (skipA2AFlow=true) ---
  delivery value:  {"status":"skipped","mode":"announce"}
  response JSON:   {"runId":"r2","status":"accepted","delivery":{"status":"skipped","mode":"announce"}}
  delivery status: skipped ✓

--- source code verification ---
  delivery declaration (line 615):
    const delivery = skipA2AFlow ? ({ status: "skipped", mode: "announce" } as const) : undefined;
  conditional spreads:   4 (expected 4)
  test results:          60 passed, 0 failed
=== ALL VERIFICATIONS PASSED ===
```

The proof exercises the same `delivery` assignment and conditional spread used in the production `sessions-send-tool.ts`. Two scenarios are covered:

1. **A2A runs asynchronously** (the common path) — `delivery` is `undefined` and omitted from the response, eliminating the misleading "pending" signal
2. **A2A is skipped** (parent-owned child session) — `delivery` preserves `{ status: "skipped", mode: "announce" }` so callers know no follow-up announcement will fire

The proof script is a standalone harness — not part of the test suite — that verifies both branches of the production code's delivery logic. It is kept in the PR body only and is not committed to the branch.

## Changes

### 1. `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.ts` — Core fix

| Aspect | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| `delivery` when `skipA2AFlow=false` | `{ status: "pending", mode: "announce" }` | `undefined` |
| `delivery` when `skipA2AFlow=true` | `{ status: "skipped", mode: "announce" }` | `{ status: "skipped", mode: "announce" }` (unchanged) |
| Return pattern | `delivery` (always included) | `...(delivery ? { delivery } : {})` (conditional) |
| Pending-error timeout response | No `sentBeforeError` field | `sentBeforeError: true` |

```typescript
// NEW — delivery is undefined when A2A runs asynchronously:
const delivery = skipA2AFlow
  ? ({ status: "skipped", mode: "announce" } as const)
  : undefined;
```

**4 return paths updated:** fire-and-forget, pending-error timeout, non-terminal timeout, success with reply.

### 2. `src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts` — 5 assertion updates

All `expect(details.delivery?.status).toBe("pending")` → `expect(details.delivery).toBeUndefined()`. The skip-case (`status: "skipped"`) remains unchanged.

## Root Cause

In `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.ts`, the `delivery` object was created as a local `const` **before** the asynchronous A2A flow started via `void startA2AFlow(...)`:

```typescript
// OLD — delivery is always defined:
const delivery = skipA2AFlow
  ? ({ status: "skipped", mode: "announce" } as const)
  : ({ status: "pending", mode: "announce" } as const);
```

Since `delivery` is a `const` captured before the async flow, `delivery.status` was **always** `"pending"` and **never** transitioned to `"delivered"`. Rather than adding a complex callback mechanism, we remove the misleading field.

## Risk checklist

- **User-visible behavior change?** Yes — but only in return metadata. Actual delivery behavior is unchanged.
- **Config, environment, or migration change?** No
- **Security, auth, secrets, network change?** No
- **Highest risk:** Code reading `delivery.status` from responses
- **Mitigation:** Field was always optional in the type; skip case preserved; 60 tests pass

## Current review state

- **Next action:** Maintainer review
- **Waiting on:** CI pipeline verification
